goal: mc owns the container runtime the gates need: `mc docker` reports the runtime, the leases on it and what it holds on disk, and `mc docker ensure` starts a stopped OrbStack (or Docker Desktop), waits until `docker info` answers and takes a lease that names a pid.

A merge round and `mc gate` start the runtime before a command gate whose selector entry says `needs: ["docker"]`, so that gate actually runs instead of reporting `unavailable`. The runner's chore pass removes leases and labelled leftovers whose holder pid is gone, and stops a runtime mc started once it has been idle for 10 minutes. The page shows all of this on one line.

Until memoro's selector emits `needs` and its Postgres script labels what it starts (a memoro proposal, not this project), the merger and `mc gate` behave exactly as today. The verb, the sweep and the page row work from the day they land.
contract: A command gate whose selector entry carries no `needs` containing `"docker"` is run exactly as today, and the exit-69 `unavailable` reading of #951 (`runSelectedCommands`, `src/mc/repo-gate.js`) stays as it is.
mc removes only Docker objects that carry the label `mc.holder` with a pid that is not alive. Unlabelled containers, volumes and images are counted and reported, never removed.

Every `docker` and `orbctl` call mc makes has a timeout. While the runtime is down, mc runs no `docker` CLI command except from `ensure`. The sweep, the page and `mc docker` with no argument read `orbctl status` and the Docker config file instead, because a `docker` call starts OrbStack.

The idle stop stops only a runtime that `mc docker ensure` started (`started_by_mc` in the state file). It never fires while a lease is alive, a dev server `listServers` reports is alive, or an unlabelled container is running.
The page stays a file reader: the docker row comes from `~/.memoro/mc/docker/state.json`, never from a command.
No file in memoro is changed by this project.
out_of_scope: Pre-pulling images (`docker_images`). `postgres:16-alpine` (412 MB) is already in the local cache.
The VM memory ceiling (`orbctl config set memory_mib`). It is already 4096 MiB on this 8 GB machine.
A build-cache cap (`docker builder prune --keep-storage`). The build cache is 0 B.

Removing unlabelled or dangling objects: today's 11 anonymous volumes (3.2 GB), the 2 exited `workerd-memoro-*-proxy` containers and the `cloudflare-dev/*sandbox` image tags. Reporting them is in scope; removing them is a later decision.
Docker in hosted CI, which already has it.

memoro's part, in `~/mc/proposals/2026-10-18-memoro-sql-reference-declares-docker.md`: `needs: ['docker']` on the `sql-reference-postgres` command in `config/testing-registry.mjs` (around line 7493) and passed through in `scripts/testing/ci.mjs`'s `--list --json` command map (around line 132); and, in `scripts/run-sql-reference-postgres.mjs` (`docker run`, around line 274), `--label mc.holder=$MC_DOCKER_HOLDER --label mc.run=$MC_DOCKER_RUN --label mc.repo=$MC_DOCKER_REPO`, plus a SIGTERM/SIGINT handler that runs its `docker rm --force --volumes`.
Stopping Docker Desktop when idle. Only OrbStack is stopped (`orbctl stop`); Docker Desktop is started, never stopped.
Checking dev servers, gate workspaces and the dependency caches against the four questions (who holds it, memory, cache, cleanup).
A dead pid reused by an unrelated process, which `pidAlive` reads as alive.

steps.title: src/mc/docker.js: the runtime, one lease file per holder, ensure and release
steps.done_when: `src/mc/docker.js` exports `dockerRoot`, `leasesDir`, `statePath`, `needsDocker`, `currentContext`, `runtimeOf`, `takeLease`, `liveLeases`, `release`, `releasePid`, `readState`, `writeState` and `ensure`, with the constants named in the instruction; the tests named in `tests/mc/docker.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-18 the memoro gate `sql:reference:postgres` exited 69 ('no Docker daemon') in 2.7 s, in two rounds, on #13803 and #13805. OrbStack is installed (`/opt/homebrew/bin/orbctl`, Docker context `orbstack`, version 2.2.4), but it was `Stopped` with `app.start_at_login: false`. memoro's probe (`dockerAvailability`, `scripts/run-sql-reference-postgres.mjs` around line 233: `docker info --format {{.ServerVersion}}`, 20 s timeout) fails at once against a stopped VM, while other `docker` calls start OrbStack themselves. Since #951 (`runSelectedCommands`, `src/mc/repo-gate.js` around line 1424) the merger reads exit 69 as `unavailable`, so the Postgres reference check has never run on the merger host. Nothing in mc starts the runtime or knows who is using it. This step is the module the next five steps build on. It adds no caller.

Create `src/mc/docker.js`. The module doc comment says what it is: the container runtime the gates need, held the way dev servers are (`dev-servers.js`). There is one lease file per holder, a dead holder's file is removed by whoever reads it next, and every call has a timeout. It says why there is no `docker` CLI call while the runtime is down: on OrbStack a `docker` call starts the VM. Imports: `randomUUID` from `node:crypto`; `existsSync`, `mkdirSync`, `readdirSync`, `readFileSync`, `rmSync` from `node:fs`; `homedir` from `node:os`; `join` from `node:path`; `writeJsonAtomic` from `./atomic-write.js`; `runTool` from `./child-async.js` (async, resolves `{ status, signal, stdout, stderr, error }`, never rejects, and `timeoutMs` kills with SIGTERM and sets `error.code` to `'ETIMEDOUT'`); `log` from `./logger.js`; `mcHome` from `./paths.js`; `pidAlive` from `./status-collect.js`.

Constants, all exported: `DOCKER_SCHEMA = 'mc-docker'`, `DOCKER_VERSION = 1`, `CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000` (any `docker` or `orbctl` call), `PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000` (one `docker info`), `START_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` (`orbctl start` or `open -a Docker`), `ENSURE_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` (the whole wait for `docker info`), `ENSURE_POLL_MS = 1_000`, `IDLE_GRACE_MS = 600_000` (used from step 5 on), and `ORBSTACK_CONTEXT = 'orbstack'`, `DESKTOP_CONTEXT = 'desktop-linux'`. Paths: `export function dockerRoot(root = mcHome()) { return join(root, 'docker'); }`, `export function leasesDir(root = mcHome()) { return join(dockerRoot(root), 'leases'); }`, `export function statePath(root = mcHome()) { return join(dockerRoot(root), 'state.json'); }`.

The machine, injectable as `dev-servers.js` and `commands/gate.js` do it. Define `const SYSTEM = { run: (tool, args, { timeoutMs }) => runTool(tool, args, { timeoutMs }), alive: pidAlive, now: () => Date.now(), sleep: (ms) => new Promise((done) => { setTimeout(done, ms); }), home: homedir(), platform: process.platform, log };`. Every exported function that touches the machine takes `{ root = mcHome(), env = process.env, io = {} }` and uses `const m = { ...SYSTEM, ...io };`. Every `m.run` call passes `timeoutMs`. Tests assert this.

`export function needsDocker(entry) { return Array.isArray(entry?.needs) && entry.needs.map(String).includes('docker'); }` reads a selector command entry (memoro's `ci.mjs --list --json` `commands[]`).

`export function currentContext({ env = process.env, io = {} } = {})` returns the context name without running anything. In order: `env.DOCKER_CONTEXT` if set; `'DOCKER_HOST'` if `env.DOCKER_HOST` is set; otherwise `currentContext` read from `join(m.home, '.docker', 'config.json')` (through `m.readFile`, default `(path) => readFileSync(path, 'utf8')`, added to SYSTEM); otherwise `'default'`. A file that is missing or will not parse gives `'default'`. On this machine the file says `orbstack`.

`export async function runtimeOf({ env, io } = {})` returns `{ kind, context, up, reason }`. `kind` is one of `'orbstack'`, `'desktop'`, `'other'`, `'none'`. For context `orbstack`: run `orbctl status` (CALL_TIMEOUT_MS). Trimmed stdout `Running` gives `up: true`, `Stopped` gives `up: false`. Any other answer, a failure or an `ENOENT` gives `up: false` with `reason` set to `orbctl status: <the last stderr line, the stdout, or the error code>`. No `docker` command is run for OrbStack. For context `desktop-linux` (kind `desktop`) and any other context (kind `other`): run `docker info --format {{.ServerVersion}}` (PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS). Exit 0 is `up: true`. An `ENOENT` error is kind `none`, `up: false`, reason `docker is not installed`. Anything else is `up: false` with the last stderr line as `reason`. Docker Desktop does not start itself on a CLI call, so this probe is safe there.

Leases. A lease file is `join(leasesDir(root), `${pid}-${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}.json`)` holding `{ schema: DOCKER_SCHEMA, version: DOCKER_VERSION, pid, run, repo, since }`. `run` and `repo` are strings or null, `since` is an ISO string. `export function takeLease({ pid, run = null, repo = null, root, io })` throws on a pid that is not a positive integer, makes the directory (`mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })`), writes with `writeJsonAtomic(path, value, { mode: 0o600 })`, and returns `{ path, lease }`.

`export function liveLeases({ root, io } = {})` reads every `*.json` in `leasesDir(root)` (a missing directory is no leases) and returns `{ leases, swept }`. `leases` is `[{ path, pid, run, repo, since }]` for files whose pid `m.alive` says is alive, oldest `since` first. A file whose integer `pid` is dead is removed (`rmSync(path, { force: true })`), logged with `m.log('docker-lease-gone', { pid, run, repo, since })`, and listed in `swept` as `{ pid, run, repo }`. A file that will not parse, or has no integer pid, is left alone and counted in neither list. When `swept` is not empty, call `writeState({ last_release_at: new Date(m.now()).toISOString() }, { root })`, because a holder that died has released.

`export function release(path, { root, io } = {})` removes that one file and returns true if it existed. When it existed, it calls `writeState({ last_release_at: <now ISO> }, { root })` and `m.log('docker-released', { path })`. `export function releasePid(pid, { root, io } = {})` releases every live lease file whose `pid` equals `pid` and returns how many it released.

State. `export function readState({ root } = {})` returns the parsed `statePath(root)` or null. `export function writeState(fields, { root, io } = {})` merges `fields` onto the current state (or `{}`), sets `schema`, `version` and `at` (now ISO), writes atomically (mode 0o600), and returns the result. Writing must never throw: catch the error and return null. The keys later steps rely on: `runtime` (`{ kind, context, up, reason }`), `leases` (`[{ pid, run, repo, since }]`), `started_by_mc` (boolean), `last_release_at` (ISO or null), `inventory` (step 2), `idle_stop` (step 5).

`export async function ensure({ pid, run = null, repo = null, timeoutMs = ENSURE_TIMEOUT_MS, root, env, io } = {})` resolves `{ ok, started, waited_ms, server, lease, reason }`. (1) `const rt = await runtimeOf({ env, io })`. (2) If `rt.up` is false: kind `orbstack` runs `orbctl start` (START_TIMEOUT_MS); kind `desktop` runs `open -a Docker` (START_TIMEOUT_MS), but only when `m.platform === 'darwin'`. Kind `none` returns `{ ok: false, reason: rt.reason }`. Kind `other` returns `{ ok: false, reason: `context ${rt.context} is not one mc can start — only ${ORBSTACK_CONTEXT} and ${DESKTOP_CONTEXT} are` }`. A start command that exits non-zero returns `{ ok: false, reason: `orbctl start failed: <last stderr line or error code>` }` (the same shape for `open -a Docker`). (3) Poll `docker info --format {{.ServerVersion}}` (PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS each) every ENSURE_POLL_MS through `m.sleep`, measuring time with `m.now()`, until it exits 0 or `timeoutMs` has passed. On timeout, return `{ ok: false, reason: `docker info did not answer within ${Math.round(timeoutMs / 1000)} s: <last stderr line>` }` and take no lease. (4) On success, `takeLease({ pid, run, repo, root, io })`. Then `writeState({ runtime: { ...rt, up: true }, leases: <liveLeases().leases without path>, ...(started ? { started_by_mc: true } : {}) }, { root })`, log `docker-ensured` with `{ pid, run, repo, started, waited_ms }` (or `docker-ensure-failed` with the reason on any failure), and return `{ ok: true, started, waited_ms, server: <trimmed stdout>, lease: <path> }`. `started` is true when step 2 ran a start command.

Tests in a new `tests/mc/docker.test.js`, in `describe('docker.js')`. Each test makes `const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'mc-docker-'))` and removes it in `finally`. Use a fake machine `fakeIo({ answers, live = [], context = 'orbstack' })`. `calls` records `[tool, ...args]` plus `opts.timeoutMs`. `run` answers from `answers`, a map from `'<tool> <args joined by space>'` to either a result or an array of results consumed in order (the last one repeats). `readFile` returns `JSON.stringify({ currentContext: context })` for `/home/u/.docker/config.json`. `home` is `'/home/u'`. `alive(pid)` is `live.includes(pid)`. `now` and `sleep` share a fake clock starting at `Date.parse('2026-10-18T12:00:00Z')`, and `sleep(ms)` advances it. `platform` is `'darwin'`. `log` pushes into `logged`. Tests: (1) 'runtimeOf asks orbctl for an OrbStack context and runs no docker command': `orbctl status` answers `{ status: 0, stdout: 'Stopped
' }`. The result is `{ kind: 'orbstack', context: 'orbstack', up: false }` (reason may be absent), and no call's tool is `docker`. (2) 'ensure starts a stopped OrbStack, waits for docker info, and takes a lease': answers are `orbctl status` Stopped, `orbctl start` `{ status: 0 }`, and `docker info --format {{.ServerVersion}}` `[{ status: 1, stderr: 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon
' }, { status: 1, stderr: 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon
' }, { status: 0, stdout: '28.0.1
' }]`, with `live: [5000]`. `await ensure({ pid: 5000, run: 'merge #7', repo: 'memoro', root, io })` gives `ok: true`, `started: true`, `server: '28.0.1'`. One file exists in `leasesDir(root)` with `pid: 5000`, `run: 'merge #7'`, `repo: 'memoro'`. `readState({ root }).started_by_mc` is true, and the calls in order are `orbctl status`, `orbctl start`, then three `docker info`. (3) 'ensure on a running runtime starts nothing': `orbctl status` Running and `docker info` 0 give `started: false`, with no `orbctl start` call and no `started_by_mc` in the state. (4) 'ensure gives up after its timeout and takes no lease': `docker info` always `{ status: 1, stderr: 'Cannot connect
' }` and `timeoutMs: 3000` give `ok: false`, `reason` matching `/docker info did not answer within 3 s: Cannot connect/u`, and an empty or missing leases directory. (5) 'a context mc cannot start is unavailable with the reason': context `colima`, `docker info` `{ status: 1, stderr: 'no daemon
' }` gives `ok: false`, `reason` matching `/context colima is not one mc can start/u`, and no `orbctl` call. (6) 'docker not installed': context `default`, `docker info` `{ status: null, error: Object.assign(new Error('spawn docker ENOENT'), { code: 'ENOENT' }) }` gives `reason: 'docker is not installed'`. (7) 'a lease whose pid is dead is removed by the next reader and counts as a release': `takeLease` for pid 5000 and for pid 41100, then `live: [5000]`. `liveLeases({ root, io })` returns one lease (pid 5000) and `swept` `[{ pid: 41100, run: null, repo: null }]`, the file for 41100 is gone, `readState({ root }).last_release_at` is `'2026-10-18T12:00:00.000Z'`, and `logged` has a `docker-lease-gone` entry. (8) 'release removes only its own file and stamps the release; releasePid releases every lease of a pid': two leases of pid 5000 and one of 6000; `release(first.path)` is true and a second `release(first.path)` is false; `releasePid(5000)` is 1; the 6000 lease remains. (9) 'needsDocker reads the selector entry': true for `{ needs: ['docker'] }`, false for `{}`, `{ needs: 'docker' }` and `{ needs: ['postgres'] }`. (10) 'every machine call carries a timeout': after tests (2) and (4), every entry in `calls` has a finite `timeoutMs`. (11) 'currentContext reads the environment before the file': `{ DOCKER_CONTEXT: 'x' }` gives `'x'`, `{ DOCKER_HOST: 'unix:///s' }` gives `'DOCKER_HOST'`, and a `readFile` that throws gives `'default'`.

Docs: create `docs/technical/mc-docker.md` with a title `# mc docker` and two sections. *The runtime and its leases* states: the lease directory `~/.memoro/mc/docker/leases/<pid>-<id>.json` with its fields; `state.json` with its keys; that a lease whose pid is gone is removed by the next reader and counts as a release; the timeouts by name and value; and that while OrbStack is down only `orbctl status` and the Docker config file are read, because a `docker` call starts OrbStack. *Why* gives the 2026-10-18 measurement from the first paragraph of this step. Later steps add sections to this file. No changelog fragment in this step: the module has no caller yet.
`mc gate tests/mc/docker.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: The verb: mc docker, ensure, release, prune
steps.done_when: `src/mc/commands/docker.js` answers `mc docker`, `mc docker ensure`, `mc docker release` and `mc docker prune`, routed by `VERB_MODULES` and listed in `src/mc/help-text.js`; `src/mc/docker.js` gains `inventory` and `removeDeadHolders`; the tests named in `tests/mc/docker-command.test.js` and `tests/mc/docker.test.js` pass, `tests/mc/help.test.js` stays green; `docs/mc-command-matrix.md` has the row in a final commit touching nothing else; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: step 1 made `src/mc/docker.js` (`ensure`, `takeLease`, `liveLeases`, `release`, `releasePid`, `readState`, `writeState`, `runtimeOf`, `currentContext`, and the constants `CALL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `IDLE_GRACE_MS` and the rest). Nothing can call it yet. Martin and the step sessions need one door to the runtime: what state it is in, who holds it, what is on disk, and a way to remove what a killed run left behind. Measured read-only on 2026-10-18: `docker system df` showed 10 images (7.5 GB, 178 tags, mostly `cloudflare-dev/*sandbox:<build>` from wrangler dev), 2 exited containers (`workerd-memoro-MediaTranscoderSandbox-*-proxy`), 11 anonymous local volumes (3.2 GB, 100% reclaimable) and a 0 B build cache. None of these carries a label, and memoro's script once leaked 113 anonymous volumes (6 GB, the comment at `scripts/run-sql-reference-postgres.mjs` around line 297). So `prune` removes only what mc labelled and only reports the rest.

In `src/mc/docker.js`, add two functions. `export async function inventory({ io } = {})` is called only when the runtime is up (callers check `runtimeOf` first) and returns `{ df, containers, volumes }`. `df` comes from `docker system df --format '{{json .}}'` (CALL_TIMEOUT_MS): one JSON object per line, mapped to `{ images: { count, size }, containers: { count, size }, volumes: { count, size }, build_cache: { size } }` from the `Type` values `Images`, `Containers`, `Local Volumes` and `Build Cache`. `count` is `Number(TotalCount)` and `size` is the `Size` string as Docker prints it (`7.519GB`). `containers` comes from `docker ps -a --format '{{json .}}'` and is `[{ id: ID, name: Names, state: State, holder }]`. `volumes` comes from `docker volume ls --format '{{json .}}'` and is `[{ name: Name, holder }]`. `holder` is the integer value of the `mc.holder=` label parsed from the comma-separated `Labels` string, or null when there is none. A call that fails or times out leaves its part empty (`df: null`, `[]`) and adds the reason to an `errors` array in the result. Then `export async function removeDeadHolders({ dryRun = false, io } = {})` takes `inventory()`, keeps the containers and volumes whose `holder` is an integer and `!m.alive(holder)`, and unless `dryRun` removes them: containers first with `docker rm --force --volumes <id>`, then volumes with `docker volume rm <name>`, each with CALL_TIMEOUT_MS. It returns `{ removed: { containers: [names], volumes: [names] }, failed: [{ name, reason }], unlabelled: { containers: <count without holder>, volumes: <count without holder>, running: <containers without holder whose state is 'running'> }, df }`. Unlabelled objects are never passed to any `rm`.

Create `src/mc/commands/docker.js` after the shape of `src/mc/commands/dev.js`: `export async function run(argv, deps = {})` and `export function usage()`, where usage returns text starting with `usage: mc docker`. Use `scanArgs` from `./flags.js` with `booleans: ['--json', '--dry-run']` and `strictValues: ['--pid', '--run', '--repo', '--timeout']`. The words are: none (status), `ensure`, `release`, `prune`. Anything else writes `mc: unknown word <w>` plus usage to stderr and returns 2. `deps` may carry `stdout`, `stderr`, `root`, `env`, `io` (passed to every docker.js call) and `ppid`, which defaults to `process.ppid`: the shell that typed the command is the default holder.

`mc docker` (status): `const rt = await runtimeOf({ env, io })`; `const { leases, swept } = liveLeases({ root, io })`; `const inv = rt.up ? await inventory({ io }) : null`; `const state = writeState({ runtime: rt, leases: <without path>, ...(inv ? { inventory: { df: inv.df, labelled: { containers: <count with holder>, volumes: <count with holder> }, unlabelled: { containers, volumes } } } : {}), ...(rt.up ? {} : { started_by_mc: false }) }, { root })`. Text output, one line each: `docker: ${rt.kind} ${rt.up ? 'up' : 'stopped'}${rt.reason ? ` — ${rt.reason}` : ''}`. Then for each lease `lease  pid ${pid}  ${run || '-'}  ${repo || '-'}  since ${since}`, or `no lease`. When `inv`: `images ${df.images.count} (${df.images.size}) · containers ${df.containers.count} · volumes ${df.volumes.count} (${df.volumes.size}) · build cache ${df.build_cache.size}` and `labelled by mc: ${c} containers, ${v} volumes · unlabelled: ${c} containers, ${v} volumes — reported, never removed`. When `rt.up`, no live lease, `state.started_by_mc` and `state.last_release_at`: `idle stop in ${Math.max(0, Math.ceil((IDLE_GRACE_MS - (now - Date.parse(last_release_at))) / 60000))} min (the runner's chore pass stops it)`. When `swept.length`: `swept ${n} lease(s) whose pid is gone`. `--json` prints `{ runtime, leases, swept, inventory, state }`. Exit 0. When the runtime is down it runs no `docker` command (only `runtimeOf`, which asks `orbctl` for OrbStack).

`mc docker ensure [--pid <n>] [--run <label>] [--repo <name>] [--timeout <s>] [--json]`: `pid` defaults to `deps.ppid ?? process.ppid`, `run` to `'mc docker ensure'`, and `timeout` to 60 s. A `--pid` that is not a positive integer, or a `--timeout` that is not a positive number, writes `mc: ...` and returns 2. It calls `ensure(...)`. On `ok`, print `docker: up${started ? ` — started in ${Math.round(waited_ms / 1000)} s` : ''} (server ${server}) — lease for pid ${pid}: ${lease}` and return 0. On failure, print `mc: docker could not be started — ${reason}` to stderr and return 69 (EX_UNAVAILABLE, what memoro's gate exits for the same fact). `--json` prints the result object.

`mc docker release [--pid <n>] [--json]`: `releasePid(pid ?? ppid, { root, io })`, then print `released ${n} lease${n === 1 ? '' : 's'} of pid ${pid}` (or `no lease of pid ${pid}`) and return 0. It stops nothing: the stop is the runner's, after the grace (step 5).

`mc docker prune [--dry-run] [--json]`: when `runtimeOf` says the runtime is not up, print `docker: ${kind} is not running — nothing to prune (mc docker prune never starts it)` and return 0. Otherwise call `removeDeadHolders({ dryRun, io })` and print `${dryRun ? 'would remove' : 'removed'} ${c} container(s) and ${v} volume(s) labelled by a holder that is gone`, one line per `failed` entry (`could not remove ${name}: ${reason}`), and `unlabelled: ${c} containers (${running} running), ${v} volumes — reported, never removed`. Return 0, or 1 when `failed` is not empty.

instruction: Why: a step session's `mc gate` on a memoro worktree runs `npm run ci -- --base-ref origin/main` as a detached child (`run`, `src/mc/commands/gate.js` around line 150), and memoro's `ci.mjs` runs the command gates itself. So on a stopped OrbStack, `sql:reference:postgres` reports `unavailable` there too: the 2026-10-18 closeout comments in memoro (`gate-flakes.json`, `mosaic-sessions.json`) both record `mc gate` red or unavailable only because Docker was down. `mc gate` answers within its budget and may exit 3 (RUNNING) while the child keeps going, so it cannot release a lease when the gate ends. The lease therefore names the child's pid, and when that pid dies the next reader removes the lease (`liveLeases`, step 1). Steps 1 and 2 made `ensure` and `needsDocker` in `src/mc/docker.js`.

Where the selection is known. `greenToRecord` (around line 179) runs the declared `select` and parses it only for a whole gate against origin/main on a clean tree. Add `docker: (Array.isArray(parsed.commands) ? parsed.commands : []).some(needsDocker),` to the `green` object it returns (around line 205). `remember` writes named fields to `gate-greens.jsonl`, so the record is unchanged. In `incrementalPlan` (`src/mc/gate-fast.js` around line 112), add `docker: commands.some(needsDocker),` to the returned object beside `commands: scripts`, importing `needsDocker` from `./docker.js`. A whole gate on a dirty tree or another base does not run the selector today and still does not: it does not ensure, and its Docker gate says `unavailable` as before. Say so in a comment.

In `run` (`src/mc/commands/gate.js`), add `dockerEnsure: (options) => ensure(options),` to `SYSTEM` (around line 64), importing `{ ensure, needsDocker }` from `../docker.js`. After `const recordable = ...` (around line 139), add `const wantsDocker = whole ? Boolean(recordable?.green?.docker) : Boolean(fast.incremental?.docker);`. When `wantsDocker`: set `childEnv.MC_DOCKER_RUN = `gate ${basename(root)}`` and `childEnv.MC_DOCKER_REPO = recordable?.green?.repo || basename(root)`, and spawn `sh -c `export MC_DOCKER_HOLDER=$$; ${chosen.run}; echo $? > '${logPath}.exit'`` instead of the plain form. `$$` is the shell's own pid, which is `child.pid`. Otherwise the spawn is byte for byte as today. After `child.unref()` and the `.pid` write, and before the lock is written, when `wantsDocker`: `const up = await io.dockerEnsure({ pid: child.pid, run: childEnv.MC_DOCKER_RUN, repo: childEnv.MC_DOCKER_REPO, root: mcHome(env), env });`. When `!up.ok`, write `mc: docker could not be started — ${up.reason}; the gate runs on, and a gate that needs docker will say unavailable\n` to stderr. When it is ok and `up.started`, write `docker: started for this gate (lease for pid ${child.pid})\n` to stderr. Nothing is released here: the lease ends with the child's pid. The ensure runs after the spawn because memoro's heavy command gates start only after the test batches, which leaves the 60 s start inside the gate's own time. Add a comment saying this.

steps.title: The runner's chore pass sweeps Docker and stops an idle runtime mc started
steps.done_when: `src/mc/docker.js` exports `sweepDocker`; `createRunner`'s `chores()` in `src/mc/run.js` calls it after `reapOrphans()` through `deps.dockerSweep` and says one line when it did something; the tests named in `tests/mc/docker.test.js` and `tests/mc/run.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: leases (steps 1, 3, 4) are removed when a reader finds their pid dead, but nothing reads them on a timer, and nothing stops the VM once the gates are done. The proposal's point is to keep the VM off between uses on an 8 GB machine that also runs the merger and the step lanes (OrbStack `memory_mib: 4096`). A killed gate also leaves its container and volume behind: `--rm` plus a forced remove does not survive SIGKILL, which is how 113 volumes piled up. Once memoro labels what it starts (a memoro proposal), these carry `mc.holder=<pid>`. The merger cannot do this sweep: `serve` (`src/mc/merger.js`) exits when its queue is empty. The runner's chore pass (`chores()`, `src/mc/run.js` around line 3133) runs on every `--idle-sleep` (default `idleSleepMs = 600_000`, around line 3247) and already reaps orphaned dev processes there (`reapOrphans`, around line 3163, through `deps.reapDevServers`, around line 512). The chore pass runs one thing after another, so a Docker call that hangs would stall archives and the nightly: every call has a timeout (step 1's constants), and while OrbStack is down only `orbctl status` runs, because a `docker` call would start the VM it is trying to keep off. Dev servers use Docker too (wrangler's `cloudflare-dev/*sandbox` containers, `workerd-memoro-*-proxy`), so a live dev server or any running unlabelled container blocks the idle stop.

In `src/mc/docker.js`, add `export async function sweepDocker({ root, env, io, servers = () => listServers().servers } = {})`, importing `listServers` from `./dev-servers.js`. Check for an import cycle: `dev-servers.js` imports `status-collect.js`, as `docker.js` does, which is fine. It resolves `{ up, swept, removed, stopped, line }`. (1) `const { leases, swept } = liveLeases({ root, io })`. (2) `const rt = await runtimeOf({ env, io })`. If `!rt.up`: `writeState({ runtime: rt, leases: <without path>, started_by_mc: false, idle_stop: null }, { root })` and return `{ up: false, swept, removed: null, stopped: false, line: swept.length ? `docker: swept ${swept.length} lease(s) whose pid is gone` : null }`, with no `docker` call. (3) `const pruned = await removeDeadHolders({ io })` (step 2). (4) Read `const state = readState({ root }) || {}` and `const liveServers = servers().filter((s) => s.live !== false)`. The runtime is idle when `leases.length === 0 && liveServers.length === 0 && pruned.unlabelled.running === 0`. (5) If idle and `rt.kind === 'orbstack' && state.started_by_mc === true && state.last_release_at` and `m.now() - Date.parse(state.last_release_at) >= IDLE_GRACE_MS`: run `orbctl stop` (CALL_TIMEOUT_MS). On exit 0, `writeState({ runtime: { ...rt, up: false }, leases: [], started_by_mc: false, idle_stop: null }, { root })`, `m.log('docker-idle-stop', { idle_ms })`, and set `stopped: true`. A failure sets the line to `docker: orbctl stop failed — <reason>`. (6) Otherwise write `writeState({ runtime: rt, leases, inventory: { df: pruned.df, unlabelled: pruned.unlabelled }, idle_stop: <ISO of last_release_at + IDLE_GRACE_MS when idle && started_by_mc && last_release_at, else null> }, { root })`. `line` is null when nothing happened. Otherwise it joins with ` · ` whichever apply: `swept ${n} lease(s) whose pid is gone`, `removed ${c} container(s) and ${v} volume(s) labelled by a holder that is gone`, `idle ${Math.round(idle_ms / 60000)} min with no lease, no dev server and no unlabelled container running — orbctl stop`, all prefixed `docker: `.

In `src/mc/run.js`, import `{ sweepDocker }` from `./docker.js`. In the real deps beside `reapDevServers` (around line 512), add `// The chore pass's Docker sweep (docker.js): dead leases, labelled leftovers, the idle stop.` and `dockerSweep: () => sweepDocker({}),`. In `chores()`, directly after `await reapOrphans();` (around line 3145), add `await sweepDockerChore();`. Define it after `reapOrphans`, after its shape: `async function sweepDockerChore() { if (!deps.dockerSweep) return; try { const outcome = await deps.dockerSweep(); if (outcome?.line) say(outcome.line); } catch (error) { say(`docker: sweep failed — ${error?.message || error}`); } }`. Give it a doc comment: a sweep failure never stops a pass; a test fixture without `dockerSweep` touches no Docker on the machine running the suite.

Tests in `tests/mc/docker.test.js` (step 1's `fakeIo`, a temporary `root`, and the `servers` option for dev servers). (1) 'with OrbStack down the sweep runs no docker command and sweeps dead leases': `orbctl status` Stopped, a lease for dead pid 41100, `servers: () => []`. The result has `up: false`, `stopped: false`, `line: 'docker: swept 1 lease(s) whose pid is gone'`; no call's tool is `docker`; `readState().started_by_mc` is false. (2) 'an OrbStack mc started, idle past the grace, is stopped': `writeState({ started_by_mc: true, last_release_at: '2026-10-18T11:49:00.000Z' })` (clock at 12:00, so 11 min idle), `orbctl status` Running, `docker system df` / `docker ps -a` / `docker volume ls` answering empty output with status 0, `orbctl stop` `{ status: 0 }`, `servers: () => []`. `stopped` is true, the calls include `['orbctl', 'stop']`, `line` matches `/docker: idle 11 min with no lease, no dev server and no unlabelled container running — orbctl stop/u`, and `readState().started_by_mc` is false. (3) 'inside the grace it is not stopped and the state says when': `last_release_at` 11:55 gives no `orbctl stop`, `stopped: false`, and `readState().idle_stop === '2026-10-18T12:05:00.000Z'`. (4) 'a live dev server holds it up': as (2) with `servers: () => [{ instance_id: 'memoro-app', live: true }]` gives no `orbctl stop`. (5) 'a running unlabelled container holds it up': as (2) with `docker ps -a` answering one `{"ID":"c1","Names":"workerd-x","State":"running","Labels":""}` line gives no `orbctl stop` and no `rm` call. (6) 'a runtime mc did not start is never stopped': as (2) with `started_by_mc: false` gives no `orbctl stop`. (7) 'a live lease holds it up': as (2) with a lease for live pid 5000 gives no `orbctl stop`. (8) 'labelled leftovers of a dead holder are removed in the sweep': `docker ps -a` lists one container labelled `mc.holder=41100`; the `rm --force --volumes` call is made and `line` matches `/removed 1 container\(s\) and 0 volume\(s\)/u`.

Tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js`, beside 'the chore pass runs the reaper every pass and says what it removed' (around line 664), with `fixture()`. (1) 'the chore pass runs the docker sweep and says its line': `f.deps.dockerSweep = async () => { passes += 1; return { line: 'docker: swept 1 lease(s) whose pid is gone' }; }`; two `runner.chores()` give `passes === 2`, and `f.files['/w/runner/log/runner.log']` matches `/docker: swept 1 lease\(s\) whose pid is gone/u`. (2) 'a docker sweep with nothing to say says nothing': it returns `{ line: null }`, and runner.log does not match `/docker:/u`. (3) 'a docker sweep that throws is said, and the chore pass goes on': it throws `new Error('orbctl status timed out')`, runner.log matches `/docker: sweep failed — orbctl status timed out/u`, and the scratch sweep still runs (assert as the reaper-throws test at around line 678 does with `f.calls.rmScratch`).

Docs: in `docs/technical/mc-run.md`, in the chores list (around lines 255-285), add item 6: `**Docker, swept** (\`sweepDocker\`, \`docker.js\`), every pass: leases whose pid is gone are removed, containers and volumes labelled \`mc.holder\` with a dead pid are removed, and an OrbStack that \`mc docker ensure\` started is stopped with \`orbctl stop\` once 10 minutes have passed since the last release with no lease, no live dev server and no running unlabelled container. While OrbStack is down only \`orbctl status\` runs; every call has a timeout; a failure is one \`docker: sweep failed\` line.` In `docs/technical/mc-docker.md`, add a section *The idle stop* with the same rules and why each condition is there (dev servers use Docker; a runtime Martin started is his). Add `changelog.d/mc-docker-sweep.md` with `section: Added` and the entry `- **The runner sweeps Docker and stops an idle OrbStack it started.** Dead leases and labelled leftovers go every chore pass; the VM stops 10 minutes after the last release, never while a dev server or an unlabelled container is running.`
`mc gate tests/mc/docker.test.js tests/mc/run.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: The page draws one docker line from the state file
steps.done_when: `collectPage` in `src/mc/page-collect.js` returns `docker` from `~/.memoro/mc/docker/state.json` (live leases only), and `renderPageLines` in `src/mc/page-render.js` draws one `docker · …` line before the MC line, nothing when the file is absent; the tests named in `tests/mc/page.test.js` pass; every `success_criteria[].met` except the two that are Martin's is true; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: the page is where Martin reads the machine, and the runtime now has state (`src/mc/docker.js`, `writeState`, written by `ensure`, `release`, `mc docker` and the runner's sweep: `runtime`, `leases`, `started_by_mc`, `last_release_at`, `inventory`, `idle_stop`). The page never runs a command ('File reads only, as DEPLOY's are: the page never runs a read', `collectPage` around line 1598), and a `docker` call would start OrbStack, so the row is drawn from the file alone. The line it draws: `docker · orbstack up · 1 lease (merge #13803) · 10 images · idle stop in 8 min`.

In `src/mc/page-collect.js`, import `{ IDLE_GRACE_MS, statePath }` from `./docker.js`. Add `export function dockerSection({ state, now = new Date(), alive = pidAlive } = {})`. It returns null when `!state?.runtime`. Otherwise it returns `{ kind, up, leases, images, idle_stop_seconds, as_of_seconds }`: `kind` and `up` from `state.runtime`; `leases` is `(state.leases || []).filter((l) => alive(l.pid))` mapped to `{ pid, run, repo }`; `images` is `state.inventory?.df?.images?.count ?? null`; `idle_stop_seconds` is `Math.max(0, Math.round((Date.parse(state.idle_stop) - now) / 1000))` when `state.idle_stop` is set, `up` is true and no lease is alive, otherwise null; `as_of_seconds` is the age of `state.at` in seconds. Give it a doc comment saying the leases are filtered by `pidAlive` because the file may be older than a holder's death. In `collectPage`'s returned object (around lines 1586-1643), add `docker: dockerSection({ state: readJson(statePath(home)), now, alive }),` after `checks`. Also add `docker` to the section list in the file's header comment (around line 23) with one line.

In `src/mc/page-render.js`, add `function dockerLine(lines, c, wide, docker)` before `mcLine` (around line 1406), drawing nothing when `!docker`. Parts joined with ` · `: `docker`; `${docker.kind === 'desktop' ? 'docker desktop' : docker.kind === 'none' ? 'not installed' : docker.kind} ${docker.up ? 'up' : 'stopped'}`; when up, `${n} lease${n === 1 ? '' : 's'}${n ? ` (${docker.leases[0].run || `pid ${docker.leases[0].pid}`}${n > 1 ? ', …' : ''})` : ''}`; `${docker.images} images` when `images != null`; `idle stop in ${Math.ceil(idle_stop_seconds / 60)} min` when `idle_stop_seconds > 0`, `idle stop due` when it is 0; and `as of ${ageWords(as_of_seconds)}` when `as_of_seconds > 3600` (`ageWords` is already used in this file). Draw it with `say(lines, c, wide, 2, text)` (grey, line 196). In `renderPageLines`, call `dockerLine(lines, c, wide, data.docker);` directly before `mcLine(...)` (around line 1514), with no blank line between them.

Tests in `tests/mc/page.test.js`, a new `describe('DOCKER — one line from the state file')` after the LANGUAGE describe (around line 506), using `pageData`, `renderPageLines`, `NOW` and `dockerSection` (add it to the import from `page-collect.js`, line 16). (1) 'is not drawn when there is no state file': `renderPageLines(pageData(), { columns: 120, now: NOW })` has no line matching `/^\s+docker ·/u`, and a page without the `docker` key draws the same lines as one with `docker: null`. (2) 'draws the runtime, the live lease, the images and the idle stop': `dockerSection({ state: { at: NOW.toISOString(), runtime: { kind: 'orbstack', up: true }, leases: [{ pid: 95259, run: 'merge #13803', repo: 'memoro' }, { pid: 41100, run: 'gate x', repo: 'x' }], inventory: { df: { images: { count: 10 } } }, idle_stop: null }, now: NOW, alive: (pid) => pid === 95259 })` gives `leases.length === 1`, and the rendered page has a line equal to `  docker · orbstack up · 1 lease (merge #13803) · 10 images` (compare after stripping trailing spaces). (3) 'an idle runtime mc started says when it stops': no leases and `idle_stop` 8 minutes after `NOW` give a line ending `· idle stop in 8 min`. (4) 'a stopped runtime is one short line': `runtime: { kind: 'orbstack', up: false }` gives `  docker · orbstack stopped`. (5) 'is gathered from the file, offline': in the style of 'is gathered from the cache and the run records, offline' (around line 563), write `join(root, 'docker', 'state.json')` with step (2)'s state (`MC_HOME: root`) and call `collectPage` with the same stubs. `data.docker.kind` is `'orbstack'`, and the `run` stub records no call whose first argument is `docker` or `orbctl`.

Docs: in `docs/technical/mc-ui.md`, in the table under *Where the facts come from* (around line 294), add the row `| the container runtime | \`~/.memoro/mc/docker/state.json\` (runtime, leases, started_by_mc, last_release_at, inventory, idle_stop) | \`mc docker\`, \`ensure\`/\`release\`, the runner's Docker sweep |`, and in *The sections* (line 45) one sentence: the docker line sits directly above the MC line, drawn only when the state file exists, from the file alone. In `docs/technical/mc-docker.md`, add a section *On the page* with the line's format. In `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`, in the `mc` row (line 28), after `a line for mc itself`, add `, a docker line from \`~/.memoro/mc/docker/state.json\` when it exists`. Put that in a final commit touching nothing else. Add `changelog.d/mc-docker-page.md` with `section: Added` and the entry `- **The page has a docker line.** The runtime, its live leases, the images and when the idle stop comes, read from the state file \`mc docker\` and the runner write; the page still runs no command.`

`mc gate tests/mc/page.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`. This is the plan's last step: in the same PR, set `success_criteria[].met` to true for every criterion in this plan except the last two (the live OrbStack check and the post-memoro merge round), which are Martin's and stay false.
